title: Scoped Execution Enablement Gate Design
claim: FP-MCP-304 defines the missing scoped execution enablement gate needed after local clearance and before any guarded runner start: execution enablement must be represented as a short-lived, single-use, exact-tuple local artifact that can make executionAllowedNow true only for one approved FP-MCP-295 guarded-run attempt, without globally disabling safety, without standing authorization, without direct HTTP execution authority, and without contacting runner start by itself.
summary: FP-MCP-303 proved the FP-027 path now reaches a valid local clearance but remains correctly blocked by GLOBAL_DISABLE_ACTIVE, RUNNER_EXECUTION_DISABLED, and OPENCODE_EXECUTION_DISABLED. FP-MCP-304 records the design contract for the missing bridge between eligible local clearance and guarded runner start. The enablement gate should be a scoped, local, short-lived, single-use artifact bound to packet, requestId, approvalId, clearanceId, modelId, runMode, workspace, branch, execution base commit, current request-artifact/evidence HEAD, pre-start evidence hash, state snapshot attempt/hash pair, and runner capability observation. It must never clear execution broadly, never create a standing global unlock, never authorize direct HTTP execution, and never start OpenCode or contact the runner start endpoint when it is created. A future guarded start may proceed only when fresh orientation reports executionAllowedNow true, preflightPassableNow true, disableSwitch passed, opencodeReadiness passed, and all prior evidence gates remain valid.
caveats: This packet is design/contract only; it does not implement the enablement tool.
No disable switch is cleared by this packet.
No runner/OpenCode execution is enabled by this packet.
Existing FP-MCP-302 approval and CLEARANCE-20260704T145411583Z-29b22ae0 should be treated as expired for any future run unless tool validation proves otherwise, and practically should be refreshed.
The exact implementation may choose different tool names, but must preserve the scoped semantics and refusal cases recorded here.
The enablement mechanism must be auditable before runner start; it must not hide enablement inside start-run.
boundaries: no OpenCode session or worker started
no MCP bridge source inspection or refactor

structuredRecord.problemStatement: FP-MCP-303 reached valid local clearance but aggregate orientation still reported executionAllowedNow false because GLOBAL_DISABLE_ACTIVE, RUNNER_EXECUTION_DISABLED, and OPENCODE_EXECUTION_DISABLED remained active. Without a scoped enablement artifact/tool, approval and clearance cycles expire at the same final blocker.

artifactStorageRules.reason: The enablement artifact is a local operator brake/release for one attempt, while admitted evidence about its creation should be recorded separately by checkpoint/result artifacts.

requiredInputs.runMode: exact allowed run mode, initially DESIGN_ONLY
requiredInputs.executionBaseCommit: commit from which execution is authorized to start, e.g. 5c0ab8b
requiredInputs.requestArtifactCommit: current clean HEAD containing request/approval/clearance evidence, must match workspace HEAD at creation
requiredInputs.preStartEvidenceSha256: hash of validated pre-start evidence artifact
requiredInputs.runnerCapabilityObservation: fresh capabilities observation proving guarded start is available
requiredInputs.expiresInMinutes: short positive lifetime no more than 5 minutes by default, hard cap 10 minutes

requiredPreconditions: ForgePilot workspace current branch matches tuple
ForgePilot workspace current HEAD equals requestArtifactCommit
request artifact exists, is valid, and remains CREATED_NOT_STARTED
request artifact model/runMode/commit tuple matches expected scope
approval artifact exists, is committed, unexpired, unconsumed, unrevoked, unquarantined, and exact-scope valid
operator-local clearance exists, is gitignored, unexpired, single-use, exact-scope valid, and eligibleForGuardedAttempt true
pre-start evidence exists and validates for the same request and approval
state snapshot evidence exists and validates for the same request
runner capabilities endpoint is reachable and advertises guarded start-run
OpenCode readiness can be checked without starting a new unbounded process
no direct HTTP execution authority is used
no existing broad or standing enablement artifact is active
refusalCases: state snapshot evidence missing or invalid
runner no longer advertises guarded start
model or run mode not allowed
existing enablement artifact uses different tuple
attempt would enable more than one request
attempt would clear global disable without scoped artifact
attempt would authorize direct HTTP execution
attempt would consume approval or contact runner start during enablement creation
sideEffectsAllowedForCreation: write or overwrite exactly one gitignored local scoped enablement artifact
postCreationValidationRequirements: verify expiration in future and within lifetime limit
verify current HEAD and branch still match
verify approval and clearance still valid
verify pre-start evidence and snapshots still valid
return eligibleForGuardedStartEnablement true only if all checks pass

interactionWithDisableSwitch.principle: The global disable switch remains a default-deny policy. The scoped enablement artifact is a narrow exception for one validated tuple, not a global state mutation.
interactionWithDisableSwitch.expectedOrientationAfterCreation: A fresh orientation should report executionAllowedNow true only when it sees valid scoped enablement plus all prior gates. It should still report globalDisableActive true as background policy if implemented that way, but disableSwitch gate should pass for the exact scoped attempt only.
interactionWithDisableSwitch.forbiddenInterpretation: Do not treat scoped enablement as permanently clearing EXECUTION_DISABLED_GLOBAL.

startMayBeContactedOnlyIf: disableSwitch gate passes for exact tuple
approval is still unconsumed immediately before start
current HEAD and workspace clean still match
runner start contact has not occurred before for this tuple
startMustConsumeOrInvalidate: approval consumption evidence only on successful guarded-start transition, according to the existing consuming-action contract
startMustRecord: runner run id or failed contact result

minimumFutureImplementationPlan: FP-MCP-305 implement scoped enablement artifact create/read/validate tools without runner start contact
FP-MCP-306 negative tests: expired approval, expired clearance, dirty tree, HEAD mismatch, stale snapshots, broad scope, duplicate enablement, direct HTTP misuse
FP-MCP-307 fresh end-to-end dry path through approval, clearance, enablement, orientation showing blockers resolved without start contact
Only after FP-MCP-307, attempt one guarded runner start if fresh orientation says executionAllowedNow true and preflightPassableNow true
